anomaly.simple: A point or period that does not fit the normal pattern of the series.
anomaly.example: A day with 10 times the usual number of orders.

z-score.simple: The distance of a value from the mean, measured in standard deviations.

standard deviation.simple: A number for how spread out values are around their mean.
standard deviation.example: Daily sales of 10, 12, 11 have a small standard deviation.

median.simple: The middle value after sorting the data.

MAD.simple: Median absolute deviation: the median of the distances from the median. A spread measure that ignores outliers.

seasonal.simple: Repeating at a fixed period, for example every 7 days.
seasonal.example: Shop sales are higher every weekend.

STL.simple: A method that splits a series into trend, season and residual using local smoothing (Loess).
STL.example: STL with period 7 on daily data.

ESD.simple: Extreme Studentized Deviate test: finds up to r outliers by removing the most extreme point step by step.
ESD.example: Generalized ESD with r = 10 and alpha = 0.05.

change point.simple: A time when the behaviour of a series changes and stays changed, for example a new mean level.
change point.example: Latency moves from 120 ms to 150 ms after a release.

CUSUM.simple: Cumulative sum: a detector that adds small drifts from a target and raises an alarm above a limit.

segment.simple: A part of the series between two change points, where the data follow one simple pattern.
segment.example: Days 1 to 49 with a mean of 10.

penalty.simple: A price paid for each extra change point, so the method does not cut too often.
penalty.example: A penalty of 10 means a cut must lower the cost by more than 10.

binary segmentation.simple: A greedy method that finds the best single cut, then repeats on each part.
binary segmentation.example: Cut at day 50, then look inside days 1-49 and 50-100.

PELT.simple: Pruned Exact Linear Time: an exact method for the best set of change points for a penalised cost.

Isolation Forest.simple: A model that isolates points with random splits. Points that are isolated quickly are anomalies.

unsupervised.simple: Learning without labels. The data has no answer column.
unsupervised.example: Finding unusual windows without a list of past failures.

autoencoder.simple: A neural network that compresses its input and rebuilds it. It is trained to copy normal data well.
autoencoder.example: A network that rebuilds 20-point sensor windows.

reconstruction error.simple: How far the rebuilt data is from the original. A large error suggests an anomaly.
reconstruction error.example: Mean squared difference between a window and its rebuilt copy.

event.simple: One anomalous period in time, with a start and an end.

point adjustment.simple: A scoring step: if any point of a true event is flagged, the whole event counts as detected. It inflates scores.
point adjustment.example: One flagged minute marks a 100-minute event as found.

NAB.simple: Numenta Anomaly Benchmark: a public benchmark whose score rewards early detection and penalises false alarms.

DTW.simple: Dynamic Time Warping: a distance between two series that allows small shifts and stretches in time.
DTW.example: Two walking recordings with a small time shift have a small DTW distance.

1-NN.simple: One nearest neighbour: give a new item the label of the closest training item.
1-NN.example: A new recording gets the label 'running' because its nearest neighbour is 'running'.

ROCKET.simple: A method that turns series into features with many random convolution kernels, then trains a linear model.
ROCKET.example: 10,000 random kernels, features max and PPV.

convolution kernel.simple: A short list of weights that slides along a series and produces a new series.
convolution kernel.example: Weights [1, 0, -1] show where the series goes up or down.

subsequence.simple: A run of consecutive points taken from a series.

matrix profile.simple: For each window of a series, the distance to its nearest other window.

motif.simple: A pattern that repeats in a series (low matrix profile value).
motif.example: The same heartbeat shape seen twice.

discord.simple: The window that is least similar to all others (highest matrix profile value). A natural anomaly.
discord.example: A broken period in a clean sine wave.

z-normalise.simple: Subtract the mean and divide by the standard deviation, so only the shape remains.
